title: Choose the texts before the questions
statement: Choose a unit's texts before its questions, each with a stated role in building knowledge of its topic, so that no text could be swapped out without changing the unit.
detail: The reading course's plan asks for a planned set of texts chosen before any question is written, each with a role such as introducing the concept, adding background, complicating it, contrasting with an earlier text, shifting genre or raising vocabulary demand, and calls it a bad sign when any text could be swapped out without changing the unit. Written feedback on an earlier build, whose texts were chosen mainly by Lexile, asked for a coherent knowledge sequence and a genre balance instead. The plan's outside orientation describes knowledge-building curricula as going deep on a topic with sets of texts and spiralling back to it in later grades with more sophistication. A proposed unit was declined because an earlier grade's unit already covered both angles it claimed as new, the mistake for which a similar unit in another grade had been retired. No unit should repeat what an earlier grade taught.

evidence.quote: A planned set of texts selected before questions are written.
Bad sign: any text can be swapped out without changing the unit.
Choose texts for a coherent knowledge sequence and a genre balance that includes poetry, drama and more literary work, and judge complexity qualitatively as well as by Lexile.
spiraling back to topic areas with more sophistication.
exact mistake for which G4's Human Body II was retired, and the G4 crosswalk already
